knowledgePattern: Check the geometric configuration before subtracting radii

hints.title: Find the centres and radii
hints.body: Complete the square in each circle equation. Write down both centres and both radii.
hints.pitfall: The number on the right is the radius squared.
hints.pause: Find the distance between the two centres.

hints.title: Check how the circles sit together
hints.body: Let the radii be R and r, with R≥r, and let the centre distance be d. Sketch the circles and join their centres. Compare d with R+r and with R−r.
hints.pitfall: A rough sketch alone does not prove whether one circle lies completely inside the other.
hints.pause: Use your exact distances to decide how the circles sit together. Then mark the closest pair of points allowed by that arrangement.

recall.reminder: Compare the distance between circle centres with the sum and difference of their radii to check how the circles meet.

solution:
1. Complete squares: C1:x2+(y−1)2=13, C2:(x−1)2+(y−2)2=5. The radii are R=13 and r=5, and the centre distance is d=2.

2. Clearly d<R+r. Also R<r+d: squaring the positive right side gives (5+2)2=7+210>13, since 10>3. Thus R−r<d<R+r, and the circles meet.

3. Choose P and Q to be the same intersection point. A length is nonnegative and this achieves zero, so the least length is 0. Answer D.
